failingTests: task 1: the form fields are controlled by state
task 2: every field has a programmatically associated label
task 3: submitting invalid input shows accessible field errors without calling the API
task 4: a valid submission posts JSON, disables Save while pending, and the new service appears
task 5: server field errors and network failures surface without losing input
task 6: editing uses PUT and deleting uses DELETE, and the list stays in sync
task 7: toasts flow through context from deep components to the layout
task 8: learner test: the form rejects a blank name

cleanup.notes: Setup (npm ci in tests/) creates tests/node_modules; the optional dev setup (npm ci in starter/) creates starter/node_modules. Cleanup deletes both; the tests create nothing else. The tests stub fetch with a fresh in-memory API per test and never use the network; the dev server's mock API resets on restart. Resetting the learner's work means restoring starter/src from a fresh copy of the lab. Test 8 is authored by the learner in starter/src/service-form.test.jsx and runs as part of the one suite; its shipped placeholder assertion fails. After the normal suite passes, npm test (tests/verify-learner-test.mjs) reruns the learner test file against runtime copies of the learner's own ServiceForm, swapped in by resolved module identity rather than import syntax: an unchanged control, which the test must pass, and six behaviour variants (blank submission ignored, blank submission calls onSave, completed submission ignored, completed submission never calls onSave, onSave receives an altered name, onSave receives an altered team), each of which the test must fail; if the labelled fields cannot be found in the submitted form, the check fails closed with its own message. This machine-scores four checks: the blank-name error appears, onSave stays uncalled for it, the completed submission is handled, and onSave receives the entered values. The use of role and label queries, user-event, the getBy/queryBy/findBy choice and the error-is-gone check are self-checked practice and not machine-verified. The check never inspects learner source text. The expected output file writes variable timings as <ms>, and test file lines may print in any order. The lab runs in two slots: tasks 1-3 in the module's S32 guided lab slot, and tasks 4-8 on S33 after that day's teach-then-check steps for create/edit/delete, submission errors and Testing Library, as interim coded practice for course-project parts P3-P5 while the course project artifact remains deferred. The 25-minute median and 30-minute cap cover the whole two-slot task set; they are planning evidence, not a measured learner pilot. Setup (the one-time npm ci) completes before the first slot's working time; the 30-minute allowance covers only work on the tasks. Public assertions are behavioral through Testing Library against rendered output and the recorded fetch calls; no test reads the learner's source text.
